answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a market or vote, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. Creating a thousand identities no longer gives an attacker free influence: every identity ties up capital, and detected abuse destroys part of it. The bond can be ferrous in its accounting trail, with a nadir threshold that limits small accounts and a plume of linked transactions triggering review; the real deterrent is the capital at risk, not the labels.
